lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: inscribing equilateral triangles, squares, and hexagons in circles
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: inscribing equilateral triangles, squares, and hexagons in circles

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: A regular quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle of radius 6. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the perpendicular bisector construction?
choices: Both constructed points are equidistant from the endpoints, and the locus of such points is exactly the perpendicular bisector.
The compass width was more than half the segment, which forces perpendicularity.
Any line through the midpoint is a perpendicular bisector.
The arcs look symmetric, so the line must be perpendicular.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a parallel lines?
choices: two lines the same distance apart at one point
two lines that meet only at infinity
two lines with the same length
two coplanar lines that never intersect, however far they are extended

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Open the compass to more than half of AB. From A draw an arc above and below AB; from B, with the same opening, draw arcs crossing them. Draw the line through the two crossing points. What has been constructed?
choices: a line parallel to AB
the perpendicular bisector of AB
the angle bisector of ∠A
a copy of segment AB

items.prompt: A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 5. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.
The construction relies on the angle being acute.
Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a line segment?
choices: the set of two endpoints and all points between them on the line through them
part of a line that goes on forever in one direction
a line with a measurable length
the shortest path between two shapes

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Through point P not on line ℓ, copy the angle that a transversal makes with ℓ, placing the copy at P on the same transversal. What has been constructed?
choices: a line through P perpendicular to ℓ
a line through P parallel to ℓ
the reflection of ℓ across P
the perpendicular bisector of the transversal

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 9. What central angle does each side subtend?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the equilateral triangle construction on a given segment?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
